Pick by the job

Three clear buying cases for the work you do most.

Most people $1,299

Aero 14

Choose it for: documents, calls, photo editing and travel with one do-everything machine.

You get: the only OLED panel, 18-hour battery and a 1.2 kg body.

Watch out: RAM cannot be upgraded and the screen is glossy.

Heavy workloads $1,899

Forge 16

Choose it for: video editing, 3D work, gaming, or sustained CPU-heavy tasks.

You get: 16 cores at 55 W, 32 GB RAM, 1 TB storage and the widest port selection.

Watch out: 2.1 kg, 9-hour battery and audible fans.

Price & battery $999

Nimbus 13

Choose it for: study, writing, web work and long days away from a charger.

You get: the lowest price, a 1.0 kg body and 22 hours of battery.

Watch out: 256 GB SSD, a 13" IPS panel and the lowest owner rating.

Bottom line. For most people the Aero 14 is worth the $300 premium over the Nimbus 13: you get an OLED screen, double the storage and the highest owner rating, with only a 0.2 kg weight penalty and 4 fewer battery hours. Choose the Forge 16 when you need its 16-core CPU, 32 GB RAM and 1 TB SSD; choose the Nimbus 13 when price and battery life come first.
